recipes.description: A ray represents a possible path of light, not a physical thread. Moving the source changes which paths reach the screen.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The barrier blocks some paths from the source, leaving a shadow. Its outline changes when source, barrier or screen moves, so the shadow alone does not uniquely reveal the object.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The small aperture admits a narrow bundle of paths. It helps separate where light comes from instead of flooding the whole screen.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The spot marks where the admitted light reaches the screen. Changing the aperture's position gives an observable test of the path model.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: In the dark room, rays from the top and bottom of the scene cross at the aperture and make an inverted image. Stray light would make that image harder to see.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: An enclosure and small opening make a portable camera obscura. This teaching construction turns a room-sized optical effect into a usable reference tool.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: At a boundary between materials, light can change direction. The simplified ray model predicts a bent path; it omits the full angle-dependent calculation.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A suitably arranged lens brings rays from a scene point toward a corresponding image point. Moving the screen away from that position blurs the image.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The aperture, source and screen can be varied and the observations repeated. The resulting evidence bears on an account of vision, not on every aspect of human perception at once.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The model connects scene points, light paths and image points. It explains the inversion without needing a picture to travel intact through the hole.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: In this modern teaching reconstruction, the optical model supplies a chosen viewpoint and picture plane. It does not claim that Renaissance perspective historically required a camera obscura.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A family of parallel lines receding from the picture plane converges toward one vanishing point in this construction. Different directions need not share that point.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The horizon and vanishing point organize a grid of receding space. The grid is a particular viewing convention, not a ranking of artistic traditions.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The courtyard plan is projected from one selected viewpoint. Change that viewpoint and a different drawing can be equally coherent.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Measured proportions connect the image to the courtyard plan. The view is now checkable, while still omitting parts hidden from its chosen observer.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Pigment supplies color and a binder holds it to the surface. Different combinations permit different marks; paint is not simply colored light.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The camera obscura supplies a reference for the courtyard's contours and light. The artist can still simplify or depart from it deliberately.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Broad light and dark masses make the courtyard legible before detail. This tonal study can support depth even without a precise geometric grid.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Tonal relationships and perspective now cooperate in the painting. Neither method alone determines what the viewer should care about.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A foreground column hides part of the wall behind it. Occlusion supplies a depth cue without requiring the viewer to calculate a vanishing point.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The courtyard has a coherent spatial reading assembled from projection, tone and overlap. The achievement is one convincing image, not a universal solution to painting.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The teaching record distinguishes the adult human lower jaw from the inherited two-part account. Age and specimen identity are recorded: adult fusion cannot be generalized to every developmental stage.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The drawing makes the observed jaw contour inspectable away from the specimen. A plate is an argument made visible, and can introduce its own distortions.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Labels connect claims to particular structures instead of to an undifferentiated picture. Readers can now point to exactly where an account disagrees.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The plates are organized for comparison. An atlas makes repeated inspection possible; its authority still depends on the observations and drawing choices behind it.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The inherited two-part lower-jaw account and the adult human observation do not match. This specific discrepancy is more useful than declaring all older medicine mistaken.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Comparing species and specimen ages asks whether an animal-based account was transferred too broadly. A difference must be located before it can support a correction.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Repeated adult-human observations support the correction in this bounded case. The historical research contrasts Vesalius's earlier Tabulae with the Fabrica; his own account changed too.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The note identifies the claim, observations and remaining limits. Correcting the jaw account does not erase Vesalius's continuing debts to Galen or certify every claim in the atlas.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: This illustrative modern calculation uses a heart rate of60 beats/minute and a stroke-volume estimate of50mL/beat: flow is3L/minute. These are teaching numbers, not a quotation of Harvey's estimates.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: At the illustrative flow of3L/minute, ten minutes gives30L passing through. Keeping units visible prevents multiplying a heartbeat count by time twice.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Thirty liters passing through in ten minutes greatly exceeds an illustrative5L blood volume. A simple one-pass consumption account would require implausibly rapid replacement; recirculation is a candidate explanation.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The supplied vein observations show flow favored in one direction. A valve can constrain movement without itself being the pump.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The vessel diagram records those directions rather than merely drawing connected tubes. It narrows which possible circulation routes fit the observations.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The heart and directed vessels form a candidate circuit. The diagram predicts a return route; drawing it is not yet observing every connection.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The circuit explains how a large throughput can coexist with a much smaller standing blood volume. This is one part of Harvey's reasoning, not a replacement for his other arguments.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Recorded interventions are compared with the circuit's predictions. Agreement strengthens this account, while the archive preserves that quantitative, experimental and analogical arguments worked together.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Malpighi's later microscopic observations, reported in1661, showed fine connections in frog tissue. These are not observations made by Harvey himself.
recipes.caveat: Later microscopic evidence is combined retrospectively with Harvey’s earlier work. Harvey did not observe these capillaries.

recipes.description: The later capillary evidence supplies an observed connection that the earlier circuit needed. The combined diagram spans different investigators and generations.
recipes.caveat: Later microscopic evidence is combined retrospectively with Harvey’s earlier work. Harvey did not observe these capillaries.

recipes.description: In this modern model an object moves from0m to6m in3s, giving average velocity +2m/s. Direction is part of velocity; a distance alone would omit it.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: For a smooth fitted position model, slopes over shrinking intervals approach an instantaneous velocity. Real sampled observations require a model and retain measurement uncertainty.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A velocity change from2m/s to8m/s over3s gives average acceleration2m/s². This finite-interval result is not automatically instantaneous acceleration throughout the interval.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A secant slope compares a curve's change in value with its change in input. Shrinking the interval asks whether those slopes approach a stable limit.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Where the limit exists, the derivative describes local change. A sharp corner is a useful warning: not every drawn curve has a derivative everywhere.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Differentiating the smooth position model produces its velocity function. This is a result about the fitted model, not direct differentiation of isolated raw measurements.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Small signed velocity×time contributions add to displacement. Traveling +6m then−4m gives net displacement2m, even though the total distance traveled is10m.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The integral is the limit of these displacement sums. To obtain total distance, integrate speed—the absolute value of velocity—instead; the distinction survives arbitrarily fine slices.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Mass times the example’s average acceleration gives its average net-force requirement in the Newtonian model. It does not by itself identify which physical interaction supplies that force.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A proposed inverse-square attraction is tested against the motion requirements and recorded orbits in this idealized Newtonian case. The candidate law supplies content that 'force' alone could not.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The next two fair rounds have four equally likely winner sequences: AA, AB, BA, BB. If the match finishes early, the unused round can still be listed to compare equally likely cases.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: In this equiprobable example, favorable cases divided by all cases gives a probability. A general sample space need not have equal probabilities; that assumption belongs to this game.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Weight each payout by its probability and add. Expected value describes an average under the model, not what any one play must pay.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: At2–1 in a first-to-three match, the leader wins unless the other player wins twice: probability3/4. Divide four coins as3 and1, not in the current-score ratio2:1.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The frequency table records repeated outcomes, including disappointing runs. A short sequence need not resemble its long-run model closely.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Relative frequencies form an empirical distribution of this record. The record can challenge an assumed model without proving exactly what will happen next.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The risk table keeps losses beside their probabilities. Equal expected values can conceal very different worst cases and matter differently to different players.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Conditioning restricts attention to cases compatible with the observed event. P(A given B) need not equal P(B given A); reversing them can change an argument completely.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: This explicitly modern extension multiplies prior odds by a likelihood ratio. Prior odds1:4 and likelihood ratio3 give posterior odds3:4—not probability3/4, and not a result from the1654 letters.
recipes.caveat: Modern Bayesian teaching extension, explicitly separate from1654.

recipes.description: The revised probabilities change the risk estimate while leaving the possible losses visible. The likelihood model and prior remain contestable; a numerical update is not manufactured certainty.
recipes.caveat: Modern Bayesian teaching extension, explicitly separate from1654.

recipes.description: The oscillator supplies a repeated motion and the escapement meters the clock's movement. A regular tick on land is only the beginning of the navigation problem.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Temperature compensation aims to reduce changes in timekeeping as conditions vary. The design must be tested; attaching the name 'compensation' does not establish its accuracy.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The mounting is intended to keep time through ship motion. Sea conditions ask a different question from a quiet workshop demonstration.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The trial log records how the timekeeper performed at sea. One good voyage still leaves durability, cost and repeatable manufacture open to examination.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: At the instant of local noon, this idealized example's reference clock reads14:00. The simultaneous difference is two hours; comparing readings from different moments would be meaningless.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Earth turns15degrees per hour, so that two-hour difference corresponds to30degrees. With the reference clock ahead at local noon, this idealized position is west of the reference meridian.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The tested timekeeper supports this clock-based fix, with its accumulated error carried forward. A reliable instrument and a correct calculation are distinct requirements.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The corrected Moon–star observation is compared with lunar tables to estimate reference time. This idealized card assumes necessary observational corrections; it is not a complete navigation procedure.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Reference sky time is compared with the ship's local astronomical time at that same observation. Local noon from another moment is not a substitute.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: In the fictional trial, clock and lunar fixes differ by2degrees. The disagreement triggers checking errors before approaching a coast; averaging them blindly could preserve a shared mistake.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The lower and upper beds record separate episodes of sediment accumulation. Their order is evidence; the section does not supply a calendar date by itself.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The older beds are now steeply tilted. Their present orientation records deformation after deposition rather than proving sediment originally fell vertically.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The tilted beds are truncated at a surface. Material is missing: erosion can leave a boundary that is positive evidence of an intervening event.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Younger beds lie across the eroded older beds at a different angle. The angular unconformity requires more than one uninterrupted episode of deposition.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The labeled section keeps the crossing relationships visible: deposition, deformation, erosion, then renewed deposition. A drawing makes the proposed event order checkable.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The crossing relationships constrain a relative chronology. They establish before and after without assigning an unsupported number of years.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Repeated ordinary processes require substantial time in Hutton's account. Siccar Point supports that reasoning; it did not create the whole theory in a single instant.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A later comparison introduces William Smith's use of characteristic fossil assemblages to recognize strata. This is not attributed to Hutton's1788 visit.
recipes.caveat: Later comparison with William Smith’s fossil mapping, not attributed to Hutton.

recipes.description: Comparing fossil-bearing sections can connect layers across a region even where surface appearance differs. Smith's1815 mapping is the historical case; any particular match still needs evidence.
recipes.caveat: Later comparison with William Smith’s fossil mapping, not attributed to Hutton.

recipes.description: The account distinguishes Hutton's event sequence from the later fossil-mapping comparison. The atlas now explains both missing time in one section and correlations between sections.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The recorded population contains differences among individuals. Treating every specimen as an imperfect copy of one ideal would discard the variation the explanation needs.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Some recorded differences recur across generations in the teaching case. Heritability, not merely visible difference, is needed for this selection model.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Individuals with a heritable difference leave different numbers of descendants under these conditions. That can change a population without any individual deciding to evolve.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A trait helpful in one environment can be costly in another. Adaptation here is a context-dependent fit, not movement toward a universal best organism.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Shared characters suggest a relationship hypothesis. Similarity can also arise independently, so resemblance alone is not an infallible family tree.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The branching diagram represents divergence, not a ladder with humans at its summit. Living branches have their own histories rather than being unfinished ancestors of one another.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A geographic barrier can reduce exchange between populations. It proposes a mechanism for divergence, but isolation alone does not determine the eventual outcome.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The island distribution is compared with a branching account and barriers. Geography becomes evidence about relationships rather than decoration around a list of species.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The fossil sequence tests whether the proposed history fits earlier forms. Incomplete preservation limits what absence can establish.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The explanation joins branching history with a possible mechanism of change. Darwin and Wallace are contributors to this case, not licenses to turn biological selection into a moral rule.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The marks locate recorded deaths; Snow’s historical map used bars. A dense cluster can reflect exposure, population density or reporting, so a map is a question-generating tool rather than a verdict.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Deaths are compared with households served. A supplier with more deaths but many more customers need not have the higher rate.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Rates are grouped by water supplier rather than just by street. The comparison now addresses a possible exposure difference.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Intermingled households help compare suppliers within shared neighborhoods. This was not random assignment; remaining household differences still deserve investigation.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A witness reports using a different water source from the one expected at the address. Interview evidence exposes a possible classification error in the neat map.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Receipts and supplier records are checked against the household account. Exposure must be established, not guessed solely from geographic proximity.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The revised exposure groups change the calculated risk comparison. A quantitative result depends on how cases and denominators were classified.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The map, interviews and rate comparison address related parts of the same question. They overlap in data and are not automatically independent confirmations.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: Alternative explanations are weighed against the exposure evidence. This supports a causal assessment while retaining observational limitations.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: A water-safety intervention can be recommended without pretending every causal uncertainty disappeared. The archive does not claim that removing one pump handle alone ended the outbreak.
recipes.caveat: Conceptual teaching relationship, not a claim that these two inputs alone historically caused this development.

recipes.description: The light-sensitive paper records exposure before a clearly visible image appears. This historical-process model describes an effect, not a chemical preparation recipe.

recipes.description: Development makes the paper negative visible. Light and dark are reversed, which will matter when another image is made from it.

recipes.description: Contact printing from the negative produces a positive image. One preserved negative makes repeat copies possible, unlike a unique direct-positive object.

recipes.description: A scale marker gives the photograph a reference for size in its plane. Perspective and camera position still limit measurements elsewhere in the scene.

recipes.description: Images taken at recorded times reveal change that a single photograph cannot. Differences in lighting or camera position can also masquerade as change.

recipes.description: Context records explain when, where and why the images were made. A photograph can be evidence without being an interpretation-free window onto the past.

recipes.description: Several prints can be made from the negative and compared by different viewers. Reproducibility changes who can inspect an image, not whether every interpretation is correct.

sources.title: Royal Museums Greenwich: Harrison and longitude

sources.title: National Gallery: perspective
sources.note: Linear perspective is one historically specific representational practice, not the culmination of all painting.

sources.title: Oxford History of Science Museum: mathematics in Islamic cultures
sources.note: Practical problems, inherited mathematics and original contributions cross languages and regions. No exclusive origin claim.

sources.title: Pascal–Fermat correspondence, 1654
sources.note: The interrupted-game problem is a case study, not the first human reasoning about chance.

sources.title: Cambridge: Newton Principia manuscript
sources.note: Mathematical recipes are modern teaching models; they do not assert the Principia was written in modern calculus notation. Newton and Leibniz developed calculus independently.

sources.title: Darwin: On the Origin of Species, first edition
sources.note: Historical primary text, not endorsement of every nineteenth-century claim; natural selection is not inevitable progress or a moral rule. Wallace is a parallel contributor.

sources.title: UCLA: Snow’s grand experiment
sources.note: Compare water companies and denominators, not merely dots on a map. Observational comparisons have limitations.

sources.title: UCLA: Broad Street outbreak context
sources.note: Do not claim a map alone revealed the cause, or pump-handle removal alone ended an already declining outbreak.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum: Talbot and photography
sources.note: Several processes and contributors; a reproducible negative differs from a unique direct-positive image. No chemical procedure is taught.

sources.title: Shannon: A Mathematical Theory of Communication
sources.note: Information-theoretic quantities do not measure truth, significance or wisdom.

sources.title: Elinor Ostrom: Beyond Markets and States
sources.note: Institutional design is contextual; neither markets, states nor commons automatically solve every collective-action problem.

sources.title: Science Museum Group: Camera Obscura
sources.note: Historical portable camera obscura object. Does not establish every recipe or an exclusive inventor.

sources.title: Cambridge Peterhouse MS209: Alhacen De Aspectibus
sources.note: A manuscript witness to the circulation of Ibn al-Haytham’s optical work. Optical recipes are modern demonstrations, not a transcription of this manuscript.

sources.title: NIST AI RMF Core
sources.note: Model validation, generalization limits and ongoing evaluation. A checklist is not a guarantee of trustworthiness.

sources.title: Francesca Schironi: Textual Scholarship in Alexandria and Beyond
sources.note: Scholar-authored research on textual practices. Modern apparatus and translation terms in this game are not all ancient Alexandrian inventions.

sources.title: American Physiological Society: history of the capillary wall
sources.note: Malpighi’s microscopic observations came after Harvey; the chapter juxtaposes distinct generations, not one experiment.

sources.title: OpenStax Calculus: net change

sources.title: Geological Society: William Smith’s1815map

sources.note: Modern Bayesian extension; not the1654 Pascal–Fermat correspondence.

sources.title: NIST LR workshop: posterior odds
sources.note: Posterior odds = prior odds × likelihood ratio, conditional on a specified model.

sources.title: Gysel: Vesalius’s Fabrica and the masticatory system
sources.note: Historical research contrasts the earlier Tabulae with the Fabrica’s account of a unified mandible. Adult anatomy; developmental fusion complicates an unqualified one-bone slogan.

sources.title: Library of Congress: printing in Asia
